conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER: The two later events flagged as ending part of the order are the Presidential notices of March 27, 2025 (90 FR 14327) and March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15511); read in full, each continues the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 for one year, lists Executive Order 13984 among the orders taking additional steps on it, and revokes nothing. They are recorded as continuation events and end no clause. The only revocation in the notices is that of Executive Order 14110 by Executive Order 14148.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13984 (January 19, 2021, 86 FR 6837) takes additional steps on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694: it directs the Secretary of Commerce to propose regulations on identity verification by United States IaaS providers and on special measures for foreign jurisdictions or persons, sets tasks for the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security, and restates the reporting authority in section 9 of Executive Order 13694. The order is operative on 2026-10-14. Its text has no sunset or revocation trigger and the held later instruments do not revoke it: Executive Orders 14110, 14144 and 14306 cite it, and the amendments of 14144 (section 9) and 14306 (section 3) are to Executive Order 13694; section 4.2(c) of Executive Order 14110 recites it and gives further directions to the Secretary of Commerce without revoking or amending it, and Executive Order 14110 was revoked in relevant part by Executive Order 14148, as the notices record; Executive Order 14117 is held only as a lead, refers to Executive Order 13694 and does not name this order. The order depends on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694, which the held Presidential notices of March 27, 2025 (90 FR 14327) and March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15511) continue; the 2026 notice lists this order among those taking additional steps and continues the emergency beyond April 1, 2026, a date after the cutoff. The held eCFR text of 31 CFR 569.201, checked as of 2026-10-14, still refers to the emergency declared in this order. The time-limited directives to the Secretary of Commerce and others are not recorded as ended: a deadline is not an ending, the held notice of proposed rulemaking (89 FR 5698) shows only the proposal step, and no held source shows final regulations, withdrawal or the reports.
